html:
1What You Will Learn

  • Describe the exam: length, format and scoring
  • Explain how single-answer and multi-select questions work
  • Plan booking, retakes and maintenance
  • Read the Body of Knowledge: 4 domains, 13 competencies, 58 indicators
  • Use the verbs of the indicators to judge how deep to study
  • Use this course: modules, tags and practice questions

2The exam: format, scoring and booking

Running case

Meet Helios

  • Helios is a fictional company of about 2,000 people that uses AI to hire and to serve customers
  • A hiring tool from the vendor Veridex screens applications
  • A customer assistant runs on a general-purpose model from Corvid Labs
  • You are the AI governance lead; Samira Haddad, the Chief AI Officer, asks you to build the program
  • Each module follows Helios one step further, in the order of the exam's own domains

The Exam at a Glance

  • 100 items, all multiple choice, with case studies
  • 2.75 hours of testing plus a 15-minute break
  • Pass mark 300 on a scale of 100 to 500
  • One point per correct answer; no essay questions
  • Taken at a Pearson VUE test center or online with OnVUE

Exam tip: The Study Guide calls it a three-hour exam. That is the 2.75 hours plus the 15-minute break, which together come to exactly three hours.

One Answer or Several: The Question Formats

  • Single answer: choose one option; the Study Guide's samples show four
  • Multi-select: the question says how many to choose (the sample shows 3 of 5); you must choose exactly that many, and there is no partial credit
  • A question can follow a scenario: you read the case, then answer questions about it
  • You can be asked to apply what you know to a situation the study material never showed
  • Every question is worth the same one point

Exam tip: On a multi-select question, the number in the stem is a rule, not a hint. Choose exactly that many options.

Scoring and Results

  • Your result is a score from 100 to 500; 300 passes
  • IAPP sets the pass mark through beta testing, expert review and psychometric analysis
  • The FAQ says all it takes is a set number of correct answers; it states no per-domain minimum
  • You see pass or fail and your score at once; an email then gives access to a section breakdown
  • IAPP does not tell you how many answers were correct, and the section percentages cannot be averaged into your score

Exam tip: Each correct answer earns one point and IAPP describes no penalty for a wrong one, so answer every question.

Booking, Taking and Keeping the Credential [Verify live]

  • Buy in the IAPP store: USD 649 for members, USD 799 for non-members
  • Schedule at least 24 hours ahead and test within one year of purchase; your profile name must match your ID
  • Test at a center or online; the break comes halfway, and the first half cannot be reopened
  • Retake no sooner than 7 days after a failed attempt, at a discounted price
  • Maintain: USD 250 for a two-year term, or membership at USD 295 a year, plus 20 credits a year
  • As of 27 October 2026: fees and rules change, so confirm them on IAPP's site before you book

Exam tip: Plan the break. Each half holds half the questions and half the time, and you cannot go back to the first half after you submit it.

3The Body of Knowledge is your scope

The Body of Knowledge Is Your Scope [Dates]

  • The Body of Knowledge (BoK) is IAPP's list of what the exam covers; this course follows version 2.1, effective 2 February 2026
  • IAPP states that no question will fall outside a topic or subtopic of the BoK
  • The Study Guide adds that a question may come from any topic listed under an area
  • The credential covers the U.S., EU and other jurisdictions
  • IAPP updates exams every year: about 10% to 15% of the content changes, and changes are announced at least 90 days ahead

Exam tip: Treat every listed topic as testable. A short bullet in the BoK can still be a question.

Four Domains, Thirteen Competencies

  • Four domains: I foundations, II laws and standards, III governing development, IV governing deployment and use
  • 13 competencies, each with a range of exam questions, and 58 performance indicators
  • Domain ranges: I 16 to 20, II 19 to 23, III 21 to 25, IV 21 to 25
  • The largest single competencies are IV.C (9 to 11) and III.C (8 to 10)

Exam tip: The ranges show weight, not a promise. A competency with a small range can still decide a close result.

How the Verbs Set the Depth

  • Every indicator starts with a verb, and the verb sets the depth of the question
  • Remember (know, define): recall the term, the list, the number
  • Understand (explain, identify): say why, how, and how it differs
  • Apply (apply, establish, perform, conduct, document): decide what to do in a situation
  • Analyze, Evaluate, Create (differentiate, assess, create): compare options and justify the choice

Exam tip: In this course a scenario question may sit above its indicator's level, never below it.

4How this course works

How This Course Works

  • 16 modules: this orientation, 13 content modules in IAPP's order, a quick-reference recap and an exam-technique module
  • Each content module has what you will learn, a Helios case check-in, Exam Tips, a recap and practice questions
  • About 30% of the questions are multi-select, as on the exam; there is no separate mock exam
  • Slide tags: Beyond the BoK (needed to answer, not in the BoK text), Dates (a date to know), Verify live (the law was still moving; shows an "as of" date)

5Your Study Plan and Ground Rules

  • IAPP advises at least 30 hours of study; study one module, then do its questions
  • Cover every indicator, because any listed topic can be asked
  • Work in order: domains I to IV, then the recap and exam technique
  • This course is independent: it is not affiliated with, endorsed by or sponsored by IAPP
  • It uses no IAPP training, practice questions or exam dumps, and it is educational, not legal advice

Exam tip: Before you book, read IAPP's current Study Guide and handbook. They outrank this course on every exam rule.
